new_reverse_pass_observations.claim: EarthScope returns response-level StationXML for all six HA10 EDH channels across the 2013 interval, but all 240 preregistered dataselect requests for the frozen June/July and September 2013 waveform windows returned HTTP 404 no-data.
The strongest direct public pre/post cross-talk discriminator selected unanimously by the JANUS council is blocked by public waveform availability rather than by a negative scientific result.
A public channel response epoch spanning 2013 does not imply that public time-series bytes are available for that epoch, and does not establish that the physical hydrophone/riser path was healthy.

whole_picture_update.instrument_lane: The published H10S fault/cross-talk history remains a live confounder. Public StationXML is static across the fault and the public pre/post waveform bytes needed for the cleanest causal test are absent at the tested 2013 windows.
whole_picture_update.2014_2015_lane: The later public waveforms still show the replicated approximately 12-13 dB H10S2-over-H10N1 broadband excess and time-variable residuals; public response correction does not remove it.
whole_picture_update.seafloor_lane: Independent native bathymetry/backscatter remains necessary because electronics cannot erase physical geometry. Direct native swath/track crossing at the frozen points is still an open gate.
whole_picture_update.causal_status: The 2013 fault cannot yet be quantified against the later 12-13 dB offset from public EarthScope pre/post waveforms because the necessary early waveform data are unavailable in this route.

claim_ceiling: This result establishes a public-data availability boundary only: response metadata exist for the six channels in 2013, while all frozen public waveform requests in this gate returned no data. It neither confirms nor falsifies the published H10S cross-talk mechanism.
